task.title: Add push and pull-request CI that cannot pass with tests silently skipped
task.description:
There is no continuous integration on push or pull request. .github/workflows/ contains only release.yml, which runs `go test ./...` at line 40 but triggers solely on v* tags. Every change that reached main so far was verified locally by one developer. Opening the project to outside contributors without CI means the first signal that a pull request broke the build is a human running the suite by hand.

Compounding this, the suite reports success while silently dropping most web client coverage when node is absent. 36 tests in internal/webui/handler_test.go begin with an exec.LookPath("node") check and t.Skip("node is required to execute the embedded client behavior") (pattern at handler_test.go:211-214). Verified at commit c453596 by running the package with node removed from PATH:

  go test ./internal/webui/ -count=1   ->  ok  github.com/dgoings/workbook/internal/webui  0.297s
  36 tests skipped

A green "ok" with the entire embedded client behavior suite skipped is the worst possible failure mode for a project whose web board just grew an optimistic mutation queue. The same silent-skip shape applies to the SHA-256 subtests, which skip when git lacks --object-format support.

Acceptance:
- A workflow runs on push and pull request against main and executes `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and gofmt verification.
- The workflow provisions node so the 36 client behavior tests run, and fails if node is missing rather than skipping.
- The workflow provisions a git new enough for --object-format=sha256 so the SHA-256 subtests run, and fails if that support is missing.
- Skips that indicate a missing capability rather than an intentionally excluded case are surfaced in the job summary, so a silently shrinking suite is visible.
- Consider running the suite on both macOS and Linux, since Workbook publishes for both and all local verification to date has been darwin/arm64 only.
